1779801719749-viuinq9.notes: University Hills' April-2026 roll is meaningfully de-risked from the prior view: Michaels and PetSmart renewed (now to 2030), so the old cluster of no-option junior boxes has largely resolved. King Soopers is locked to 2044 (stability, not upside), leaving Office Depot's Sep-2026 expiry with no options as the one genuine near-term mark-to-market/re-leasing lever, plus a small ~3,500 SF vacancy.

1779801655754-6fobrpj.notes: Vestavia Hills (previously ungraded) is 92.4% occupied as of April 2026, anchored by Publix with options running to 2047 and showing healthy recent restaurant/service leasing. The offsets are ~7.6% vacancy to lease, non-investment-grade AMC theater exposure, a near-term Movement Mortgage office rollover, and the 1954 vintage — netting to a solid B+.

dealScore.rationale: Monopoly-position enclosed mall in a small Indiana market; durable in its trade area but format- and demographics-challenged.
strengths: Only enclosed mall within ~50 miles; ~97.7% occupied with a deep tenant roster
Confirmed ~482,000 SF total (resolves the prior 309k vs 482k size discrepancy)
National junior anchors (Best Buy, Burlington, Ross, PetSmart, Five Below) plus Target/Dunham's/Aldi
risks: Anchors are deeply below market (Target $1.70, Dunham's/Aldi $4.70) but heavily optioned — not a mark-to-market source
Enclosed-mall format in a small, lower-income market; many tiny/temporary (TAW) tenants inflate the occupancy count
Near-term rollover: Books-A-Million (2027), Best Buy and Ross (2029)

1779798205645-4ncqs4b.notes: Markland Mall's April-2026 roll confirms ~482,000 SF total (resolving the earlier size discrepancy) and ~97.7% occupancy, though the count includes many tiny kiosk/temporary tenants. Target, Dunham's and Aldi pay almost nothing ($1.70-$4.70/SF) but each holds long option stacks, so those rents are tenant-controlled and not a realistic mark-to-market opportunity. The structural challenge remains the enclosed-mall format in a small, lower-income trade area.
